title: Finite-token UX hypotheses & micro-PRD
content:
Context:
I keep running into product/UX needs where customers want predictable token spend for interactive flows (dialogs, assistants, form-filling). Hosted pricing + per-token metering is powerful but too opaque for many app teams. This doc is a compact brainstorm of ideas for a lightweight UX and behavior model that lets end-users and developers reason about "finite" token budgets per conversation while preserving responsiveness and quality.

What problem are we solving?
- End apps need predictable token spend for user-facing workflows (esp. chatbots, on-site assistants, support flows).
- Developers want a small set of knobs to trade cost vs quality without deep infra changes.
- End users get surprised by slow responses or degraded quality when we apply aggressive fallback policies mid-conversation.

High-level concept: Token Envelopes + Graceful Fidelity Ladder
- Token Envelope: a soft-per-conversation token budget (N tokens) that depletes as assistant generates tokens. Envelopes can be created by developer or suggested by system heuristics.
- Graceful Fidelity Ladder: defined tiers of model fidelity (full, compact, compressed, metadata-only) with mapping to token budgets and degradation strategies.
- UX indicators: simple UI affordances that inform users of remaining envelope (like a progress bar + micro copy) and allow explicit top-ups or switch to a low-cost summary mode.

User stories (dev and end-user focused)
- As a product owner, I want to cap average tokens per conversation at 150 so our monthly hosting bill is predictable. Acceptance: dashboards show avg tokens/convo and alerts when avg exceeds threshold.
- As an end user, I want to know when continuing the chat will cost more so I can choose to shorten my query. Acceptance: inline message when envelope < 20% with option: "Trim response" or "Continue (use 50 extra tokens)".
- As an engineer, I want a single API flag to attach an envelope to a request so we can test without changing model configs. Acceptance: API has 'token_envelope': {"limit":150, "policy":"graceful"} and server enforces soft behavior.

Behavioral primitives (backend) - rough ideas
- Charge-on-generate accounting: count tokens as we stream; stop at envelope limit and emit a controlled truncation event.
- Soft-limits vs hard-limits: soft-limit triggers ladder step (switch to compact model/measure), hard-limit stops generation and returns a "need more tokens" code.
- Prefix caching awareness: prefer using cached prefixes to reduce envelope consumption for commonly repeated system prompts.
- Progressive compression: when envelope is below threshold, compress internal context (summarize older turns) to free budget.

UI sketches (copy only)
- Inline microcopy: "Low budget — we’ll send a short summary unless you allow 50 more tokens."
- Progress bar: mini pill near chat header: [■■■■■■■■□□] 120/200 tokens
- Quick actions: +50 tokens, Auto-summarize, Use full fidelity (confirm)

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0: Internal beta — implement envelope flag and basic soft-limit truncation. Collect metrics on truncated responses and developer feedback.
- Phase 1: Developer opt-in — expose UI components in SDK (progress pill, actions) + telemetry hooks. Start with hosted small customers.
- Phase 2: Auto-suggestions — platform recommends envelope sizes per route based on historical token distribution.
- Phase 3: Enterprise controls — allow org-level default envelopes, billing alerts, SLA interactions.

Metrics to watch (signal + guardrails)
- Avg tokens per conversation (targetable by developer).
- % conversations truncated by envelope (should be < 2% for default conservative envelopes).
- User action rates on top-up CTA (indicates friction).
- Conversion/retention delta when envelope UX is shown vs hidden.

Open questions / trade-offs
- UX risk: Will surfacing token budgets confuse end users? Mitigation: keep microcopy simple and focus on choice (short answer vs full).
- Billing model: Do we charge for attempted tokens beyond envelope if user top-ups mid-generation? Need billing policy.
- Model selection rules: How aggressive to be when switching fidelity? We need cost profiles and quality baselines per model.
- Prefetching vs envelope accounting: If we precompute suggestions for quick replies, do we charge envelope? (Prefer not)

Implementation notes / dev hints
- API shape idea: request param 'token_envelope.limit' (int), 'token_envelope.mode' (soft|hard), 'token_envelope.fallbacks' (list of model ids in fidelity order)
- Telemetry: emit events token_envelope.started, token_envelope.topup_requested, token_envelope.truncated, token_envelope.fallback_used
- Starter fallback set: [redwood-1-lg, redwood-1-sm-quant, redwood-summary-compact] — map later to real catalog ids.

Next steps (short)
- Quick spike: implement counting+soft truncation in local dev runtime, demo with two sample bot flows. Owner: Samira. Timebox: 3 days.
- Small UX test: build progress pill component in playground and test with 5 internal users for clarity. Owner: Clara. Timebox: 1 week.
- Meet with billing/product to align on top-up billing semantics. Owner: Ravi.

Notes to self (scratch)
- Keep naming simple: 'budget' may read better than 'envelope' for some PMs. Test both.
- Consider per-turn vs per-conversation envelopes. Some apps require per-turn caps (forms).
- Think about server-side composition with caching so short answers don't eat budget.

Rough acceptance checklist for MVP
- API supports envelope param and server enforces token accounting.
- SDK exposes a basic progress pill + top-up callback.
- Telemetry emitted for envelope lifecycle events.
- Demo flow that shows graceful fallback to compact model and compression of old turns.

End of notes — keeping this intentionally compact. Will iterate after internal spike and UX probe.
